name: Mercury
fact: Surface temperatures swing 610°C in a single day. No atmosphere — just raw exposure to space.
bio: The smallest planet. Its highly elliptical orbit (e=0.206) makes it accelerate noticeably near perihelion. Despite being closest to the Sun, Venus is hotter.

science_sections.why: Mercury's 0.206 eccentricity is the highest of the 8 planets — at perihelion the Sun appears 1.5× larger in its sky than at aphelion.
The perihelion-aphelion swing (46–70 million km) drives huge differences in solar flux — Mercury's surface heats and cools more than any other planet.
Vis-viva is what shows Mercury speeding up dramatically at perihelion and slowing at aphelion — a 12 km/s swing.
Mercury's axial tilt is essentially zero (0.034°), so the bottoms of polar craters never see sunlight — and water ice survives there despite the planet's heat.
Three missions span Mercury's exploration: Mariner 10 (1974), MESSENGER (2011–15), and BepiColombo (orbit insertion late 2026).
